Build the full functionality for Prompt Forge exactly as specified below. Implement robust front-end state management plus a secure client-side / serverless API layer for handling API keys and generation requests. Persist settings (API keys, prefix/suffix, custom instruction) but never persist uploaded images to the server (images remain client-side/session-only unless the user explicitly downloads or saves them). Provide real-time validation and friendly error messages for all user inputs.

Global behavior & security:

Authentication: optional seed for later; for MVP allow local session storage of settings. All API keys must be stored encrypted in browser storage or in a serverless safe store — document how to swap to a secure backend later.

Multi-model selection: allow the user to add multiple provider API keys and choose which model to use per generation. Models to surface initially (user-provided):

Google Gemini family: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (Standard), Gemini 3 Flash (Latest), Gemini 3 Pro (High Quality), Gemini 2.5 Flash (Lite) and Gemma 3-12b / 3-4b / 3-2b / 3-1b where available.

Groq Cloud family: Llama 4 Scout Fast, Llama 4 Mavertick HQ.

Mistral AI family: Pixtral 12B Vision.

Additionally: the UI must fetch and include available free Mistral text-only models and Groq text-only models at runtime by querying those providers’ model listing endpoints (do not hardcode only — detect and present current model names).

Model fallback and usage-limit handling: if the currently selected model reports a usage limit or error during generation, do not fail silently. Pause the current attempt, show a persistent header notification that reads: “Usage limit reached for [Model]. Change model to continue.” Provide inline quick actions to switch to another available model (Groq / Mistral / Gemini) and automatically change the primary generation button to Regenerate. After user selects another model and clicks Regenerate, resume the generation from where it paused. Keep robust retry and error handling.

Section 1 — Image → Prompt generator:

Upload UX: support bulk JPEG/PNG uploads via drag-and-drop or Add Images button. Show image thumbnails with filename, resolution, and a remove icon. Allow reordering images.

When user clicks Generate: for each uploaded image, send the image (or a secure image reference) to the selected vision-enabled model(s) to extract a rich, detailed, stock-ready prompt. The returned prompt must be complete and explicit, containing every relevant visual detail (composition, lighting, color palette, camera lens/angle if detectable, subject details, textures, clothing/props, background details) so the user can re-create near-identical stock images with other AI image models. Do not include unnecessary special symbols.

Output formatting rules: one clear paragraph per prompt, no bullet lists, no superfluous special characters, numbered lists only if absolutely necessary. Keep language concise and professional. Support multi-language input but outputs must be in English unless user explicitly chooses another language.

CSV export: after generation, show a popup with header text Download Your CSV Prompts and a Download button. Generate a CSV with columns at minimum: SL No., Image Filename, Prompt. Each row corresponds to one input image, prompts in the Prompt column. (If you must support alternate CSV shapes, also provide a version where each image’s prompt is a separate column with headers Image1_Prompt, Image2_Prompt, etc., but default to one-row-per-image for compatibility.) Filename the CSV promptforge_prompts_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv.

Section 2 — Prefix & Suffix manager:

UI to add one or multiple prefix and suffix strings. When generating prompts, the tool prepends prefixes and appends suffixes to each generated prompt. Prevent exact duplicates — if the user pastes the same prefix twice, ignore duplicates and show a small inline warning. Allow the user to control how many prefixes/suffixes are applied and the order (drag-to-order). Support a count slider to repeat a prefix/suffix up to N times if user chooses.

Section 3 — Clear Data:

Provide a prominent Clear Data button that removes all uploaded images, generated prompts, and resets in-memory session state. If the user has unsaved settings, do not clear saved settings. Confirm via small toast modal: “Clear all uploaded images and generated prompts? This cannot be undone.”

Section 4 — Refine your prompt like a prompt engineer:

A dedicated tool labeled Refine your prompt like a prompt engineer. Input can be in any language or poorly-formed. The tool will translate (if not English), clean grammar, remove extraneous special characters, and output a single powerful English paragraph written like a professional prompt engineer. No bullets, only paragraph form (numbering allowed if helpful). Use the selected text models (Gemini family, Groq, Mistral) for refinement. Enforce the same model fallback behavior described above.

Section 5 — Custom Instruction:

Global Custom Instruction field where the user can enter a custom prompt snippet or instructions. When present it becomes a global modifier applied to all model calls (image-to-prompt and refine). Show a UI summary “Custom Instruction active” when populated.

Section 6 — Save All Settings:

A Save All Settings button saves API Keys (encrypted), prefix/suffix lists, custom instruction, preferred default model, and UI theme; do not save uploaded images. After saving, show a small non-blocking notification: “Settings saved.” Provide an option to export/import settings as a JSON file for backup.

Section 7 — Community Hub:

A Community Hub button that opens a modal or dedicated page containing the following links and contact information formatted as clickable links:

Join Our Microstock Free Support Group: Whatsapp Number: +88 01881-447666

Subscribe To My Channel: https://youtube.com/@MasterWithShawon

Join Our Group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/masterwithshawon

Follow Me: https://www.facebook.com/itsmdshawon/

Section 8 — Footer & legal:

Footer must include exact text © Copyright 2026 PromptForge. All Rights Reserved and links to Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions, and FAQ pages. Provide simple, clear templates for Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions, and an FAQ relevant to Prompt Forge usage (privacy, API key storage, image handling). Show “Developed by Md. Shawon” which links to https://www.behance.net/itsmdshawon.

Extra UI/UX & behavior details:

Disable any generation output that contains forbidden special symbols; sanitize outputs prior to showing/saving.

Provide copy-to-clipboard for each generated prompt, and a “copy all” that copies prompts as CSV or as separate paragraphs.

Show progress and per-image status during batch generation with an overall progress bar. Allow canceling in-flight generation.

Accessibility: add ARIA labels, keyboard shortcuts for main actions (Upload, Generate, Clear Data, Save All Settings).

Logging & debugging: add an optional developer console output panel (collapsible) that logs model responses and errors (do not log API keys).

API & integration notes for developer:

Document how to plug in provider APIs (Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral): include example request payloads, expected response shapes, and how to stream partial responses if available. Provide sample serverless endpoints that proxy requests to providers so API keys never appear in client code.

Model discovery: implement a small runtime utility to call provider model-list endpoints (where available) and populate dropdowns with up-to-date model names (this meets the requirement to include free text-only Mistral and Groq models dynamically).

Testing: include unit tests for CSV generation, prefix/suffix logic, and model-fallback flows.

Final deliverable:

Complete Vite-ready project generated in Vibe Code format, with clear folder structure, components, and documentation. Include sample environment files and instructions to deploy to Vercel. Ensure the UI and generated CSV content exactly match copy/paste-ready requirements above.

**Considering Available Models**

I'm currently focused on the model integrations for "Prompt Forge." I'm prioritizing Google's Gemini, and also investigating Groq Cloud's dynamic model discovery. Mistral AI is on the list as well. The goal is to provide a broad range of options for users to generate prompts.


**Developing Feature List**

I've been refining the feature list for "Prompt Forge." Key additions include bulk image upload with drag-and-drop, detailed image-to-prompt generation, and CSV prompt export. I'm also working on a prefix/suffix manager, custom instruction capabilities, and a prompt refiner. I'm thinking about session-only data clearing, saving settings, adding a community hub and footer links.


**Enumerating Model Capabilities**

I'm now fully immersed in the model integrations and structuring the associated files. The planned modules are taking shape: `metadata.json`, `index.*`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, and `services/aiService.ts`. I am considering which models to enable such as Gemini and Mistral, and how to accommodate fallback or mock behaviors. Furthermore, I've got to consider encryption so I might implement a simplified encryption strategy for demo-level API key storage as requested.


**Initiating Development Phase**

Now, I'm diving into the building phase, with core features prioritized. I'm focusing on batch image generation, using an iterative approach to process images, and text-to-text calls for refinement. For the CSV generation, I am aiming to use a dedicated utility function, and have decided to start construction on all of these. I am also planning on a standard encryption strategy.

entries.description: Optimized Groq execution speed by adding client-side image resizing (to 800px) specifically for vision tasks to drastically reduce payload size and upload time. Combined system instructions into the user prompt for Groq to optimize the LLM's attention mechanism and bypass potential role-switching overhead. Reduced max_tokens for Scout Fast to 256 for near-instant responses. Streamlined the retry logic to remove unnecessary delays on the first few attempts.

Implemented parallel processing for batch generation to remove internal queuing. The application now processes images concurrently with a limit, significantly reducing total batch time while maintaining UI responsiveness.

Help & FAQ Content:

Help & FAQ

What is Prompt Forge?
Prompt Forge is a tool that helps you turn images into clear, ready-to-use prompts. You can use these prompts with AI image generators to create new images easily.

How does Prompt Forge work?
You upload one or more images. The tool looks at the images and creates full prompts based on what it sees. You can then copy and use those prompts anywhere you like.

Which AI models does Prompt Forge support?
Prompt Forge works with multiple AI models from Gemini, Groq, and Mistral. You can choose the model you prefer before generating prompts.

Do I need my own API keys?
Yes. You need to add your own API keys in the settings so the models can work properly.

Can I upload multiple images at once?
Yes. You can upload many images together using drag and drop or the Add Images button.

What are Add to Start and Add to End?
These options let you add text at the beginning or end of every generated prompt. This helps keep your prompts consistent.

What are Negative Words?
Negative Words let you block specific words so they never appear in any generated prompt, no matter which model you use.

Is my data safe?
Your images and prompts are used only to generate results for you. Prompt Forge does not take ownership of your content.

Can I clear all data?
Yes. The Clear Data option removes uploaded images and generated prompts so you can start fresh.

What should I do if something does not work?
First, check your API keys and settings. If the problem continues, try refreshing the page or reloading the tool.
